edits.old: Then the log line holds neither the token nor the reference value
edits.new:
Then the log line holds neither the token nor the reference value

  Scenario: AC13 The view v_ace_contact of party "P-0077" errors and is refused with 503 naming the ACE database, and nothing is guessed from a cache (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the v_ace_contact view of party "P-0077" returns an error
    When rwb-comms calls GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/contact-points?personKey=P-0077&channel=MOBILE
    Then the answer is 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming the ACE database
    Then no cached contact point is returned

  Scenario: AC14 A result append is refused with 503 while the delivery columns are missing and no entry with a null reference is written (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the delivery columns of interaction are missing because the letter slice of this key has not migrated
    When rwb-comms appends the result of "NSS-7781" with status "READ" and a new Idempotency-Key
    Then the answer is 503 with MSG-GEN-006
    Then no interaction entry with a null external reference exists

  Scenario: AC15 A caller without the right to read contact points is refused with 403 and the log holds neither the token nor the contact value (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a caller holds no right to read contact points in rwb-access
    When the caller calls GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/contact-points?personKey=P-0077&channel=MOBILE
    Then the answer is 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then the log line holds no token and no contact value

  Scenario: AC16 A request with no credential is refused with 401 and a caller without the right is refused with 403 on each provided operation (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a request to GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/contact-points and a request to POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions carry no credential
    When rwb-comms calls each of the two operations without a credential
    Then the answer is 401 on each operation and no row is returned or written
    Then a caller without the right is answered 403 on each operation as in AC10 and AC15
